gate0.notes: This is a per-layer subsection (not a full Blueprint). It is structurally complete relative to the per-layer Design contract for the cc layer: it carries frontmatter (doc_type, feature_slug, scope_class, layer_scope, derived_from, companion_artifacts, generated, generated_by, inherited_adrs); declares the chosen §6 option (§2); states rationale (§2 three reasons + §2.1 rejection rationales); enumerates conventions touched (§3 8-row table covering all 8 PRD inventory items + the 1 outside-inventory file with explicit AC-FR-4-a treatment); details implementation in cc primitives (§4 dispatch section content; §5 schema closure; §6 cleanup); presents Sub-Agents (§7), Skills (§8), Hooks (§9), CLAUDE.md (§10), MCP (§11), Naming (§12), Error states (§13); produces 10 EARS-format ACs (§14 — AC-CC-1..10); surfaces 6 Q-CC items for composer (§15) + 5 OI-CC items (§16); declares dependencies (§17) backed by cc-dependencies.json. cc-dependencies.json conforms to the per-layer dependency schema (intra_layer_dependencies, cross_decision_dependencies, inherited_adrs_consumed, f7_constraint, open_items_surfaced_to_composer).

verdict.summary: pass — proceed to Design Composition. The cc-design selects §6 option (a), grounds it in three load-bearing reasons aligned with synthesis D-001, preserves the four specialist-isolation invariants, honors F-7 via the two-session pattern, and correctly inherits ADR-0017 + ADR-0033 (not ADR-0034) for the 4-cycle cap + symmetric D-12. Two MAJOR findings (I-DR-001 incomplete ADR-0034 sweep on execute-finalize-reconciler; I-DR-002 inconsistent treatment of the execute-orchestrator description line citing 'symmetric application per D-12') and several MINOR/NIT items are flagged for design-composer awareness but do not block composition. The Q-CC-1 divergence from synthesis D-005 is well-rationalized (MINOR — composer ratifies).
conditions: Design composer or plan-author MUST address I-DR-001: the ADR-0034 mis-citation on execute-finalize-reconciler.md appears on lines 3 (description), 19 (Authoritative references), 82 (section heading), 84 (body). cc-design §6 only corrects line 19. Per synthesis Constraint 5.4 (DISSENT-2 carry-through), all four occurrences must be corrected.

Design composer to evaluate I-DR-002: execute-orchestrator.md:3 description ends with 'symmetric application per D-12' but does NOT cite ADR-0034. This is technically correct but design-composer should confirm whether any inheriting ADR or comment elsewhere implies ADR-0034 as the source.

Design composer ratifies the Q-CC-1 divergence from synthesis D-005 (Designer recommends authoring the Agent-grant ADR in this feature vs. synthesis defer recommendation). Designer's rationale is reasonable; composer's call.

Grep confirms ADR-0034 also appears on: line 3 (description, 'symmetric ADR-0017 application per ADR-0034'); line 82 (section heading 'Cycle-cap escalation (D-12 + ADR-0034)'); line 84 (body 'When... ADR-0017 + ADR-0034'). Per synthesis Constraint 5.4 / OI-FRAMER-1 (DISSENT-2 carry-through), every reference to ADR-0034 as the symmetric-D-12 source must be corrected to ADR-0033.
issues.suggestion: Update §6 (D-003) edit list to include all 4 ADR-0034 references on execute-finalize-reconciler.md (lines 3, 19, 82, 84). Update AC-CC-5 wording to cover the full sweep. Plan-author can elect to make all 4 corrections a single atomic edit. Design-composer should confirm the same sweep was applied to plan-author's task scope.

issues.description: execute-orchestrator.md:3 description ends with 'symmetric application per D-12' — does NOT explicitly cite ADR-0034 (good — no mis-credit) but also does NOT cite ADR-0033. Under the §6 option (a) re-framing where execute-orchestrator becomes an advisor, the description line is a documentation surface that downstream readers will use to understand the state-machine reference; explicit ADR-0033 citation would close the propagation loop completely.
issues.suggestion: Consider adding an edit in §6's edit list (or §3's Conventions Touched body re-framing for execute-orchestrator) to append '(per ADR-0017 4-cycle cap + ADR-0033 symmetric D-12 application)' to execute-orchestrator.md:3. Low-cost edit; closes DISSENT-2 carry-through completely on the advisor file.

issues.description: The cc-design diverges from synthesis D-005.1 by recommending authoring the project-wide ADR ('sub-agents MUST NOT declare Agent in tools lists') in THIS feature. Synthesis explicitly defers this work (RICE=0.625; scope-creep risk; user-memory preference cited). The Designer's rationale ('T-001's 3-source citation work + D-003 cleanup are both in this run; deferring re-incurs source-citation work') is reasonable but the divergence is load-bearing for design-composer's ADR-authorship scope under FR-5 / FR-8. AC-CC-10 is explicitly conditional on Q-CC-1 disposition; if composer defers, AC-CC-10 drops.
issues.suggestion: This is well-rationalized divergence — MINOR for the divergence itself. Surfaced as IMPORTANT because design-composer's ADR-authorship scope (single ADR for D-001 vs. two ADRs for D-001 + the convention) determines plan-author task count and the Blueprint's adrs_authored frontmatter. Design-composer should ratify explicitly and the Blueprint should record the decision in the Fact Disposition Table or composer rationale. The divergence itself is acceptable; the open question is the composer's call.

issues.description: The cc-design specifies WHAT the new Execution Phase Dispatch section contains (§4 — 7 numbered content items) and WHAT the schema-closure edit covers (§5 — three new fields + void/-prime extensions). Both edit the same file (recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md). Per synthesis Constraint 5.1, these two edits MUST be sequenced coherently — recommended D-004 schema closure first, then D-001 dispatch section absorption. The cc-design notes 'plan-author MUST sequence them coherently (synthesis Constraint 5.1)' at §5 closing but does NOT name the recommended order. plan-author may pick the inverse order.
issues.suggestion: Either: (a) cc-design §5 explicitly names the recommended order (schema closure first, then dispatch-section absorption) per synthesis substrate Constraint 5.1's interaction analysis (D-001 ↔ D-004); OR (b) flag this as an explicit Q-CC-N item for design-composer/plan-author arbitration. Currently the design defers the sequencing without naming the recommendation. Low-effort fix.

issues.description: §13 covers four error states (advisor file missing, specialist missing, checkpoint malformed, log_state_transition.py failure). It does NOT cover the case where the new 'dispatch_directives[]' array in quality-reconciliation-log.json is malformed or missing under the new D-003 re-framing — which is a novel failure surface introduced by this feature. Under option (a), the parent reads dispatch_directives[] to invoke targets; if the reconciler emits an empty or malformed array, the parent has no fallback documented.
issues.suggestion: Add an error-state entry for malformed/empty dispatch_directives[] under §13. Plan-author can decide the parent's behavior: surface to user, fall back to a default dispatch, or treat as cycle-cap-equivalent escalation. Mentioning the constraint in this Design unblocks plan-author from inventing it ad-hoc.

issues.description: Q-CC-3 surfaces execute-orchestrator.md:7 declaring 'recipe-feature-pipeline' in its own skills: array. The Designer recommends preserving with body-prose rationale. Under option (a)'s advisor re-framing this seems sensible. However, ADR-0022's SA-13 BLOCKER check (per codebase-analysis OQ-CR-003) may flag self-references; the rationale should be encoded as a body comment in execute-orchestrator.md (so future SA-13 audit passes have explicit evidence of intentionality) rather than only in the Q-CC narrative.
issues.suggestion: If composer ratifies preserve (option b in Q-CC-3), require an explicit body-prose comment in execute-orchestrator.md (e.g., near line 7 or as a 'Skills rationale' subsection) documenting 'recipe-feature-pipeline in skills: is intentional — this advisor file documents the state machine the parent skill orchestrates'. This converts the rationale from Q-CC-narrative to file-resident evidence for SA-13 audits.

issues.description: The cc-design (§2.2) correctly notes that 'No new sub-agent files are authored by this feature. Existing sub-agents are edited only.' This makes F-7 vacuous for this feature's own implementation. However, AC-CC-6 still imposes the session-restart constraint conditionally on plan-author's synthetic test design (FR-6). The AC wording is correct but the contingency creates uncertainty: if plan-author elects a no-new-agents synthetic test (e.g., reusing existing specialists with a probe task), AC-CC-6 is vacuously satisfied; if plan-author authors a new test-specific agent, the constraint fires. Cross-artifact reviewer should verify this contingency at the plan + test-artifact stage.
issues.suggestion: No fix required at cc-design stage. Flag for cross-artifact-audit-reviewer (downstream): verify plan-author's synthetic-test design either declares 'no new agents' (vacuously satisfies AC-CC-6) or includes the explicit session-restart step. Recorded here for traceability.

issues.location: cc-design.md §3 Conventions Touched table row 8 (state-transitions.log per-entry schema)
issues.description: The §3 table row 8 describes the change as '(outside-inventory; 1 file → AC-FR-4-a open-item count = 1)' but the cell content describes BOTH the v1 invariant clarification AND folding in the void/-prime extensions. These are TWO distinct semantic changes packaged as one row. PRD AC-FR-4-a counts files, not edits — so 1 file is correct — but design-composer should be aware the file edit is more substantive than 'a single clarification'.
issues.suggestion: Either split into two rows (one for the invoking_agent invariant clarification per §5; one for the void/-prime extension folding per §5) OR add a sub-bullet under the existing row enumerating both sub-edits. This clarifies the Fact Disposition Table the design-composer will build.

issues.description: The reasoning-configuration table preserves all 5 specialists' triplets unchanged. Under option (a)'s re-framing, execute-orchestrator becomes an advisor — it is no longer dispatched at runtime. ADR-0022 governs SA-13 audit at runtime invocation; a never-invoked agent's reasoning triplet has no operational effect. The §7.1 row for execute-orchestrator labels the verdict 'PRESERVED, but see Q-CC-3' — this is correct but does not address whether opus/high is still warranted for an advisor that is never invoked. The conservative answer is 'preserve to keep the file invocable if option (a) is reversed' — but this should be explicit.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief footnote under §7.1 row 1: 'Triplet preserved despite advisor role — option (a) reversal would require re-invocation; preserving the triplet keeps that reversal cheap.' One sentence. Closes the latent question.

issues.description: cc-design.md frontmatter declares 12 inherited ADRs (ADR-0017, 0019, 0021, 0022, 0027, 0029, 0033, 0035, 0036, 0037, 0040, 0041). cc-dependencies.json inherited_adrs_consumed lists the same 12. Codebase-analysis.json identifies ADR-0035, ADR-0042, ADR-0043 as 'newly_surfaced_adrs_not_in_research_plan_list' for design-composer review. ADR-0035 IS inherited (good — picked up). ADR-0042 and ADR-0043 (auditing-mcp family graduation + Gate-6 hard gate) are NOT in the inherited list. Codebase-analysis notes 'These ADRs ALSO reference the execute-* agents... Likely UNLIKELY to constrain the dispatch repair, but design-composer should confirm.' The cc-design does not document its disposition of ADR-0042/0043.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) add a brief disposition note in cc-design (e.g., a new sub-section under §2.2 or in §15 Q-CC-N) explaining why ADR-0042/0043 are NOT inherited (likely because they constrain the auditing-mcp Gate-6 step which is orthogonal to dispatch); or (b) inherit them defensively. The cc-design subsection should not leave this gap for design-composer to resolve without context. Codebase-analysis OI-CR-E surfaces this; the cc-design should close it.

issues.description: cc-dependencies.json lists 7 intra_layer_dependencies (parent skill → 4 specialists, parent skill → advisor reference, parent skill → log_state_transition.py). Schema conforms to the per-layer dependency schema. All targets exist in the codebase (verified via Glob). However, the dependency on auditing-shared/scripts/log_state_transition.py is correctly characterized as 'bash_invocation' — but the broader auditing-shared skill binding (which would inherit ADR-0035 discipline) is not captured. The 4 specialists currently have skills: [..., auditing-shared] (for the reviewer/handler/reconciler) which IS the binding ADR-0035 covers.
issues.suggestion: Optional: add a row to cc-dependencies.json's intra_layer_dependencies capturing 'specialists → auditing-shared skill' as kind: 'skill_binding'. This makes the ADR-0035 inheritance evidence-backed in the dependencies artifact rather than only frontmatter-declared. Low-priority; design-composer can elect to incorporate.

issues.description: AC-CC-8 and AC-CC-9 specify cycle-counter increment behavior + cap exhaustion. These are inherited from PRD NFR-3-a and NFR-3-b. The cc-design correctly identifies that under option (a), the parent orchestrator owns the counter (in checkpoint.json.execution_pipeline_cycle_counters). However, AC-CC-8 says 'parent orchestrator shall increment' but does not specify which transition increments which counter (the inherited invariant from execute-orchestrator.md:43 is that ONLY T4 and T10 increment, NOT T0/T13). This invariant is load-bearing per I-AA-609 and is documented in execute-orchestrator.md and state-transitions-log-entry-template.md but not propagated into the new AC.
issues.suggestion: Append to AC-CC-8: 'specifically at T4 (per-task NEEDS_REVISION) for per_task counters and T10 (phase reconciliation cycle complete) for per_phase counters — per I-AA-609 invariant 10. T0 and T13 boundary transitions are logged but do NOT increment.' This propagates the I-AA-609 invariant into the new ACs.
